## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by relatively large, flattened cells divided into two symmetrical semicells by a deep central constriction. Each semicell has broadly rounded lateral lobes, a distinct apical lobe with a deep central notch, and prominent surface ornamentation, including basal tubercles and pore fields. Euastrum crassum occurs primarily in acidic, nutrient-poor freshwater habitats, especially shallow bog pools and other humic wetlands with slight mineral influence. Like other desmids, it contributes to primary production and can serve as an indicator of oligotrophic, acidic water conditions.
